flows.name: Visit landing page
flows.goal: Understand what StudioDesk is for and get started.

steps.userAction: The visitor opens the StudioDesk landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that StudioDesk is one calm workspace for a solo freelance designer to run clients, projects, and bookings, and offers to sign up, sign in, or open the public booking page.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up as the designer.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-up screen.

alternatives.condition: The visitor chooses to sign in instead.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-in screen so the visitor can sign back in.

alternatives.condition: The visitor chooses to open the public booking page instead.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the public booking page with session types and open slots.

flows.outcome: Nothing is stored; the visitor reaches sign-up, sign-in, or the public booking page.

flows.name: Designer signs up
flows.goal: Create an account and reach the home screen.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty designer auth form.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the designer auth form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the account, signs her in, and shows the home screen with today's sessions, follow-ups due this week, and overdue tasks.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is missing or not valid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the account fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The email is already registered.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the email already has an account and offers to sign in instead.

flows.outcome: A new designer account exists and sign-in persists; after refresh she is still signed in on the home screen.

flows.name: Designer signs in
flows.goal: Sign back in to the workspace.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty designer auth form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the designer auth form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website signs her in and shows her home screen with today's sessions, follow-ups due this week, and overdue tasks.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is missing or not valid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Signing in fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is incorrect.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the sign-in did not match and keeps what was typed so it can be corrected.

flows.outcome: The designer is signed in and stays signed in after a refresh.

flows.name: Designer signs out
flows.goal: Leave the workspace securely.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website signs her out and shows the public landing page.

flows.outcome: The designer is signed out; a refresh still shows the signed-out landing page.

flows.name: Add a client
flows.goal: Remember a new client for the first time.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client list sorted with overdue follow-ups first, then soonest, then no date.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty client form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the client form and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the client and shows it in the client list in its sorted position.

alternatives.condition: No clients exist yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says there are no clients yet and offers to add the first client.

alternatives.condition: The designer cancels.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is saved; the website shows the client list as it was.

alternatives.condition: A required value is missing or not valid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: The new client is saved and still appears in the client list after a refresh.

flows.name: View clients and handle follow-ups
flows.goal: See who needs a follow-up and act in one click.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows clients sorted with overdue follow-ups first, then soonest, then no date, with overdue highlighted and one-click actions to mark done or push a week.

steps.userAction: The designer marks a follow-up done with one click.
steps.websiteResponse: The website clears that client's follow-up date and updates the sorted order.

steps.userAction: The designer pushes a follow-up a week with one click.
steps.websiteResponse: The website adds seven days to that client's follow-up date and updates the sorted order.

alternatives.condition: No clients exist yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says there are no clients yet and offers to add a client.

alternatives.condition: Marking the follow-up done fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the follow-up date unchanged and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: Pushing the follow-up a week fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the follow-up date unchanged and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: Follow-up dates updated by done or push-a-week persist and the sorted order still shows after a refresh.

flows.name: Edit a client
flows.goal: Keep a client's details and follow-up date up to date.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client list sorted with overdue follow-ups first.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client's name, email, company, profile, status, and follow-up date.

steps.userAction: The designer edits the client details and saves them.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the changes and shows the updated client in its sorted position.

alternatives.condition: No clients exist yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says there are no clients yet and offers to add a client.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.

alternatives.condition: A required value is missing or not valid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The designer cancels.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is changed; the website shows the client again as it was.

flows.outcome: Client changes are saved and still show after a refresh.

flows.name: Delete a client
flows.goal: Remove a client and everything under it.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client list sorted with overdue follow-ups first.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client's details with its projects and notes.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on the client.

alternatives.condition: No clients exist yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says there are no clients yet and offers to add a client.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.

alternatives.condition: The designer confirmed the deletion.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the client list without the deleted client, its projects, tasks, and notes.

alternatives.condition: The designer cancelled.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is deleted; the website shows the client again, unchanged.

flows.outcome: The client, its projects, tasks, and notes are gone and stay gone after a refresh.

flows.name: Add and view client notes

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client from the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client's details with its dated notes newest first and its follow-up date.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a note.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty note form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the note date and text and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the note and shows it with the client's notes in date order.

steps.userAction: The designer sets or changes the follow-up date and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the follow-up date and shows it on the client.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on a mistaken note.

alternatives.condition: There are no notes under the client yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the client with no notes yet and offers to add the first note.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.

alternatives.condition: The note date is missing or the note text is empty.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the note fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The follow-up date is not a valid date.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the date and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the follow-up date fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed date and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The designer confirms the deletion.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the client with its remaining notes, without the deleted note.

alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is deleted; the website shows the client notes unchanged.

flows.outcome: New notes and the follow-up date are saved under the client and still show after a refresh.

fields.label: Designer email
fields.meaning: Email the designer uses to sign up and sign in

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret that proves the designer owns the account

fields.label: Client name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the client

fields.label: Client email
fields.meaning: Email used to contact the client and to match bookings

fields.label: Company
fields.meaning: Client company, when the client has one

fields.label: Profile
fields.meaning: Short profile of what the client does, how they met, and what they pay
fields.example: Runs a D2C store, met at a design meetup, pays per project

fields.label: Client status
fields.meaning: Whether the client is a Lead, Active, or Past

fields.label: Follow-up date
fields.meaning: When the designer should next follow up with the client

fields.label: Note date
fields.meaning: The day the call or note happened

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: What was discussed or decided after a call
fields.example: Discussed homepage rework, will share wireframes next week

fields.label: Project name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the piece of work

fields.label: Project description
fields.meaning: Short summary of what the project covers

fields.label: Project due date
fields.meaning: When the project should be finished, if there is a deadline

fields.label: Task title
fields.meaning: What needs to be done in the project

fields.label: Task status
fields.meaning: Whether the task is To do, In progress, or Done

fields.label: Task priority
fields.meaning: How urgent the task is: Low, Medium, or High

fields.label: Task due date
fields.meaning: When the task should be finished, if there is a deadline

fields.label: Available days
fields.meaning: Which weekdays the designer can be booked

fields.label: Available from
fields.meaning: Start of the bookable window on each available day

fields.label: Available to
fields.meaning: End of the bookable window on each available day

fields.label: Session type name
fields.meaning: How the bookable session is presented to bookers

fields.label: Duration in minutes
fields.meaning: How long one session lasts

fields.label: Price display
fields.meaning: Price shown for information only, or Free; nobody pays in the app

fields.label: Maximum people
fields.meaning: How many bookings a slot accepts before it is full

fields.label: Booker name
fields.meaning: Name of the person booking a session

fields.label: Booker email
fields.meaning: Email of the person booking, used to link to a client

fields.label: Search tasks
fields.meaning: Free text to find tasks by title inside a project

fields.label: Chosen session type
fields.meaning: Which kind of session the booker wants to book

fields.label: Chosen slot
fields.meaning: The specific date and start time the booker picks

fields.label: Task status filter
fields.meaning: Which task statuses to show inside a project

fields.label: Task priority filter
fields.meaning: Which task priorities to show inside a project

steps.websiteResponse: The website asks to confirm the deletion and says what else will be removed with it.

alternatives.condition: The user confirms.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website deletes the record and what belongs to it.

alternatives.condition: The user cancels.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is deleted; the record stays as it was.

assumptions.text: Notes are append-only history: the designer can add and view notes and delete a mistaken note, but cannot edit a note's date or text after saving, to keep call history trustworthy.

The project list is sorted by project due date soonest first, with projects without a due date last, then by name. Inside a project, overdue tasks are highlighted and task filters default to showing all statuses and priorities.

Until the designer sets weekly availability, the public booking page shows no open slots and explains that no times are available yet. Availability changes apply to future slot generation only and never move or cancel existing Sessions or Bookings.
